job_description.title: Marketing Intern
job_description.purpose: Provide summer campaign delivery capacity for the Brand Marketing team as the summer campaign calendar has increased.
job_description.business_impact: Support delivery of weekly campaign content and TikTok posts for summer campaigns.
responsibilities: Draft and schedule weekly campaign content with the team.
Script and film short TikTok videos with the team.
outcomes: Within first 30 days, Deliver three approved TikTok posts each week.
Within first 90 days, Support one full campaign cycle end to end.
Within by internship end, Publish a reusable summary of campaign results and learnings.

must_have_criteria.text: Script and film short TikTok videos with the team.

preferred_criteria.text: Use a basic visual editing tool to prepare social assets.

company_behaviours.role_behaviour: Shares draft work early and incorporates feedback when a campaign draft receives feedback.

logistics: Internship role in Brand Marketing within Consumer Products.
Must hold valid New Zealand work rights.
assessment_expectations: Structured screening questions assess approved role requirements.
Candidates may use academic, volunteer, extracurricular, personal-project, or work evidence.
Portfolio examples are discussed but do not replace human review.

screening_questions.question: Describe a short TikTok video you have scripted and filmed with other people. What was the brief, what did you personally do, and what was the result?
screening_questions.purpose: Assess direct, owned evidence of scripting and filming short TikTok content collaboratively.
expected_evidence: A specific short-form video example from work, study, volunteer, extracurricular, or personal-project experience.
The candidate's personal contribution to scripting and filming.
How they worked with others and the resulting output or response.

rubric.description: States they have not scripted or filmed a short TikTok video and provides no equivalent short-form video evidence.
Provides no relevant example or does not describe any scripting or filming activity.
Gives a generic or indirect example, with unclear personal ownership of the script or filming.
Describes a relevant short-form video with a clear personal contribution to scripting and filming and some detail on team involvement.
Provides a specific TikTok or comparable short-form example, clearly explains script and filming actions, collaboration, and a concrete output or result.
Provides a detailed, validated example with clear ownership of scripting and filming, collaboration choices, measurable or documented outcomes, trade-offs, and reflection on improvements.

green_flags: Explains both scripting and filming rather than only appearing in or posting a video.
Clearly distinguishes personal actions from team actions.
Connects creative choices to the intended audience or campaign brief.
red_flags: Says others created the script or filmed the content without describing an equivalent personal contribution.
Cannot explain what they personally did.
Provides an unrelated example with no short-form video production evidence.
screening_questions.follow_up: What specific decisions did you make in the script and during filming, and why?

screening_questions.question: Walk us through how you would turn a campaign idea into a short TikTok video with a team, from first draft through filming.
screening_questions.purpose: Assess practical understanding of the workflow required to script and film team-based TikTok content.
expected_evidence: A logical sequence from campaign idea or brief to a short script and filmed asset.
Consideration of roles, timing, and coordination with team members.
Specific actions the candidate would take during scripting and filming.

rubric.description: Describes an approach that omits both scripting and filming, or explicitly cannot explain how to create a short TikTok video.
Provides no relevant workflow or only repeats that they would make a video.
Offers a generic sequence with little connection to scripting, filming, or team coordination.
Outlines a relevant workflow covering a campaign idea, a basic script, filming, and some team coordination.
Gives a clear, practical end-to-end workflow with defined scripting and filming steps, coordination points, and attention to a concise TikTok format.

Gives a detailed workflow that anticipates trade-offs, assigns or clarifies team contributions, includes efficient iteration, and explains how the final filmed asset would be checked against the campaign idea.

green_flags: Breaks the work into actionable scripting, filming, and coordination steps.
Recognises that short-form content needs a clear, concise concept.
Identifies when to involve teammates before filming.
red_flags: Focuses only on publishing or scheduling and omits content creation.
Cannot describe a script or filming process.
Assumes team members will complete key work without clarifying their own contribution.
screening_questions.follow_up: Where would you seek input from the team before filming, and what would you do with that input?

screening_questions.question: Tell us about a time you shared a draft video or script early and received feedback. How did you decide what to change before filming or finalising the content?
screening_questions.purpose: Assess the approved Collaboration behaviour in the context of producing TikTok content.
expected_evidence: A specific draft script, storyboard, video, or comparable content example.
Evidence that the candidate shared work early and sought or received feedback.
Clear changes made in response to feedback and the resulting outcome.

rubric.description: Says they do not share drafts or explicitly rejects incorporating feedback on content work.
Provides no example of sharing draft content or responding to feedback.
Mentions receiving feedback but gives no specific draft, changes, or personal role in the process.
Describes a relevant draft content example, feedback received, and at least one personally owned change.
Provides a specific example of sharing a draft early, explains how feedback was evaluated and incorporated, and describes the resulting improvement to the content.

Provides a detailed example with early feedback timing, clear ownership, rationale for accepting or adapting feedback, resulting content outcomes, and reflection on how the process improved later work.

green_flags: Shares work before it is final.
Can explain which feedback led to specific changes.
Distinguishes useful feedback from changes that did not fit the brief.
red_flags: Describes refusing or disregarding relevant feedback without a work-related rationale.
Cannot identify any personal changes after feedback.
Gives only a vague statement that they are open to feedback.
screening_questions.follow_up: What feedback did you not use, if any, and how did you decide?

screening_questions.question: Tell us about a visual social asset you edited using Canva or a comparable tool. What did you personally change, what feedback did you apply, and what was delivered?
screening_questions.purpose: Assess owned evidence of basic visual content editing without requiring prior paid work.
expected_evidence: A specific visual asset from work, study, volunteering, or a personal project.
The editing tool and changes personally completed.
Feedback incorporated and a concrete delivered result.

rubric.description: States they have not edited a visual asset and provides no comparable evidence.
Provides no relevant visual editing example or personal contribution.
Names an editing tool or asset but gives only a generic account with unclear ownership.
Describes a relevant asset, a personally completed edit, and a delivered output.
Provides a specific example with clear editing ownership, feedback applied, and a concrete result.
Provides externally verified editing evidence with clear ownership, trade-offs, results, and reflection.

green_flags: Clearly distinguishes personal edits from supplied material.
Explains how feedback changed the delivered asset.
Uses an equivalent academic, volunteer, or personal project.
red_flags: Names a tool without describing any actual edit.
Attributes all editing decisions and execution to others.
Provides no concrete delivered visual output.
screening_questions.follow_up: Which edit had the greatest effect on the final asset, and how did you decide?

screening_questions.question: If you were asked to help create three approved TikTok posts in a week, how would you organise your scripting and filming work with the team?
screening_questions.purpose: Assess whether the candidate can apply scripting and filming capability to the role's weekly TikTok delivery outcome.
expected_evidence: A practical plan for developing and filming multiple short TikTok posts.
Prioritisation of scripting, filming, team coordination, and review activity.
Awareness that content needs approval before delivery.

rubric.description: Proposes no scripting or filming activity, or states they could not contribute to producing the posts.
Provides no workable plan for producing short TikTok content with the team.
Gives a generic plan with no sequencing of scripts, filming, team coordination, or approval.
Outlines a workable weekly plan that includes scripting and filming multiple posts with some team coordination.
Gives a specific, feasible plan that sequences scripts, filming, feedback or review, and team coordination to support three approved posts.

Provides a detailed plan with prioritisation, contingencies for delays or rework, clear individual and team actions, and an explanation of how approval feedback would be incorporated while maintaining delivery.

green_flags: Plans for scripts and filming before final approval.
Breaks work into manageable steps across the week.
Accounts for coordination and review with the team.
red_flags: Treats approval as unnecessary or assumes posts can be delivered without review.
Offers only broad statements about being organised.
Does not include any scripting or filming actions.
screening_questions.follow_up: How would you respond if feedback required one of the planned posts to be revised late in the week?

human_review_guidance: Verify examples through specific actions, ownership, context, and outcomes rather than confidence or presentation style.
Consider equivalent evidence from academic, volunteer, extracurricular, and personal projects appropriate to an internship role.
Assess the approved requirement and observable collaboration behaviour only; do not use personality, social similarity, or writing polish as proxies for capability.
Use the rubric consistently, record evidence and uncertainties, and keep progression or rejection decisions with human reviewers rather than making them autonomously.
